title: Add guided RAG walkthrough templates with synthetic corpora and deterministic eval hooks
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce interactive RAG walkthrough templates that include a synthetic-corpus generator, deterministic eval hooks, and telemetry probe presets for local authoring and CI smoke tests.
body:
Context and motivation: This PR adds a set of guided RAG walkthrough templates aimed at developer onboarding and reproducible local testing. The goal is to provide small, deterministic end-to-end scenarios (index -> retrieval -> agent/tool-calls -> final answer) that teams can run locally and in CI to validate routing, embeddings, tool binding, and structured-output assertions. These templates target both new users (guided step-by-step) and infra teams (deterministic eval hooks and telemetry presets for cost/latency probes).

What this PR includes: - Four new walkthrough templates under quickstarts/walkthroughs/: 'customer-support', 'policy-extractor', 'sales-summary', and 'local-qa' — each with a short README, a tiny synthetic corpus generator, and a one-command local runner. - A lightweight synthetic-corpus generator (scripts/generate_corpus.py) that produces seeded, small index files in JSONL. The generator supports size=small/medium and seed to ensure reproducible retrievals. - Deterministic eval hooks (walkthroughs/_eval/) that assert model outputs against golden prompts using a seeding strategy for any randomness (temperature=0 for CI, seeded RNG for local dev). - Playwright-based smoke scenarios (ci/smoke/walkthroughs.spec.ts) to run a headless quickstart flow in CI and assert telemetry emits. - Telemetry presets and probe docs (walkthroughs/telemetry-presets.md) that include examples for Redwood Console probes: token counts, per-request latency, and tool invocation counts. - Updated quickstarts index and docs nav entry so these templates appear under "Local authoring & quickstarts" on the docs site.

Design notes and trade-offs: - Synthetic corpora are intentionally tiny (~5-20 docs) to keep CI fast and low-cost. They include adversarial edge-cases (overlapping entities, short identical passages) to exercise reranker and retrieval heuristics. - Eval hooks are intentionally strict in CI (temperature=0, deterministic embeddings seed) which will fail if model or retrieval regressions occur. For local runs, authors can switch to temperature>0 to explore. - The Playwright smoke test checks end-to-end flow and the presence of telemetry events; it is intentionally minimal to avoid flakiness.

Checklist:
- [x] Add walkthrough templates and READMEs
- [x] Add synthetic corpus generator with seed support
- [x] Add deterministic eval hooks and golden outputs
- [x] Add telemetry preset documentation
- [x] Add CI smoke tests and Playwright scenarios
- [x] Update quickstarts index and docs nav
- [x] Add unit tests for corpus generator and eval harness

Commits summary: - a2f8b3c: initial walkthrough templates and generator stub - 6c4d2e9: flesh out customer-support and policy-extractor walkthroughs - 92b1f77: add deterministic eval hooks and golden outputs - d4e5a7a: add Playwright smoke tests and CI job - e8c9aa0: docs nav and telemetry presets

Files changed (high level): - quickstarts/walkthroughs/customer-support/README.md - quickstarts/walkthroughs/customer-support/run.sh - quickstarts/walkthroughs/policy-extractor/README.md - quickstarts/walkthroughs/local-qa/README.md - quickstarts/walkthroughs/sales-summary/README.md - quickstarts/walkthroughs/_eval/ (golden outputs and assertion harness) - scripts/generate_corpus.py - ci/smoke/walkthroughs.spec.ts - quickstarts/index.md (nav entry) - walkthroughs/telemetry-presets.md - tests/test_generate_corpus.py - examples/sample_corpora/*.jsonl

Small illustrative snippet (corpus generator seed usage):

# generate_corpus.py --seed 42 --size small --out examples/sample_corpora/customer_support_seed42.jsonl

The generator produces short JSONL docs with stable IDs so retrieval results are stable across runs when the same seed is used.

Review conversation snapshot: Miguel Torres (reviewer) - "Nice addition. Two things I'd like to see before merge: 1) clarify how the CI secrets are consumed by the Playwright smoke job; 2) reduce the Playwright timeout for the smoke check (it currently waits 30s which is too long for our fast CI)."

Asha (author) - "Thanks Miguel — addressing both: updated CI job to read REDWOOD_CLI_TOKEN from repo secrets and added a 10s explicit wait/timeout for the smoke assertion. PTAL."

Leah Kim (reviewer) - "Eval hooks are great. Suggest we add a short note in the README that these are intentionally strict in CI and how to relax them locally."

Asha (author) - "Added a 'Running locally' section to each README and examples showing temperature/seed override. Also added a note in telemetry-presets.md."

CI summary: - Initial run: lint + unit tests passed, Playwright smoke failed intermittently (timing issue). - Rerun after changes: all checks passed. CI artifacts: attached smoke run logs and trace files.

Performance and cost considerations: The smoke CI job targets a 40s wall-clock budget and the synthetic corpora keep token usage < 4k per run. Telemetry presets include token counts and a per-route cost estimate to help authors iterate on cost.

Migration and rollout: This is additive; no migration required. The docs nav update will surface these templates in the next docs site build.

Follow-ups planned: - ENG-1429: add examples that show cache warmup patterns with prefix caching. - PM-88: gather qualitative onboarding feedback from two internal teams and refine templates. - Add a periodic CI job to run walkthroughs against a dedicated lightweight model variant (low-cost) to detect regression without incurring high tokens.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-20 after approvals from Miguel and Leah. CI green at merge.

Contact: If you have questions or want additional walkthroughs (e.g. multimodal examples), ping @asha or open an issue under quickstarts/walkthroughs.
